nodes.label: Triage Router
nodes.rationale: Cost-control admission controller: six agents on every utterance would be ~3.2M input tokens per meeting-hour; the router keeps 80-90% silent-pass so only named agents wake.

nodes.label: Decision Record
nodes.rationale: The single durable output and compounding moat; carries an unconfirmed→confirmed→superseded lifecycle so Falcon never cites its own unratified or reversed decisions.

nodes.label: Org Decision Index
nodes.rationale: The compounding retention asset the moat depends on; why a workspace won't churn at month nine.

nodes.label: F6.5 Directed Question Detection
nodes.rationale: A directed question owes a direct private answer, not a proactive tip; addressee ('you') resolved from conversational context, waking every plausible candidate when ambiguous rather than guessing wrong.

nodes.label: F7.1 Direct-answer Mode
nodes.rationale: premise_challenged is a confidence-scored claim; its 1-turn fast-path collapses Gate 2 only when corroborated by a second independent signal — one judgment escalates attention, two escalate action.

nodes.label: F7.2 Untrusted Input Isolation
nodes.rationale: Delimiters aren't injection-proof, so the real defense is provenance-gated output: gate on retrieval, not on generation — an agent can be tricked into saying something but cannot manufacture a valid artifact ID it never retrieved.

nodes.label: F8 Coordinator Intervention Gates
nodes.rationale: Gate 3 is the product's spine: if Falcon knows nothing the humans don't, it stays silent — preference disagreements belong to humans. A turn counts entrenchment (restate/defend after pushback), not speech rhythm.

nodes.label: F9.1a Publish-time ACL Intersection
nodes.rationale: Retrieval-time ACLs protect each agent's own lookups, but the shared card crosses that boundary — so ACL is re-enforced at publish time against the intersection of all recipients (cite / abstract / route-to-private-nudge). A genuinely new, non-negotiable security boundary.

nodes.label: F9.2a Blame-neutral Synthesis
nodes.rationale: An accurate but socially harmful fact on a room-wide card is a report being blindsided in front of peers — the kind of moment that gets a tool banned company-wide; performance-adjacent signals are nudge-only.

nodes.label: F10.1 Decision Records with Truth-state
nodes.rationale: A wrong remembered decision is worse than a forgotten one; only human-ratified (confirmed) records enter the retrievable index — human-in-the-loop on the write path because it feeds the read path.

nodes.label: §12.1 Latency Budget
nodes.rationale: ≤7s total; real-time feel lives on the tail, so the high-variance stages (STT and the two LLM calls) are the ones to protect. Mitigated by speculative pre-computation of the card at escalation-eligibility.

nodes.label: §12.2 COGS per Meeting-hour
nodes.rationale: VAD gating and the triage router carry the <$2/meeting-hour number: without VAD, STT cost multiplies ~sevenfold; without triage, agent cost multiplies tenfold.

nodes.label: §12.3 Reliability & Security
nodes.rationale: Open Thread state is event-sourced (not snapshotted) to a Redis Stream synchronously before any transition commits, so a crash mid-argument can't silently reset a thread one turn from triggering a card.

nodes.label: §12.5 Resilience Architecture
nodes.rationale: Right-sized for stage: cheap high-value fixes built first; two heavier mechanisms (continuous semantic sequencer, warm-standby shards) deferred until real load justifies them — don't harden before validating the product.

nodes.label: §12.6 Load & Cost Governance
nodes.rationale: Backpressure and cost overrun are the same event in two units (latency vs dollars); one lever — the triage router's load-adaptive salience threshold — governs both. Correctness (merge) never degrades before coverage.

nodes.label: §12.7 Evaluation Harness
nodes.rationale: You cannot tune what you cannot measure; Phase 0 recordings become the labeled golden set so no judgment-layer change reaches production on vibes, and G3's 70% precision is measured rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: §12.8 Model Governance
nodes.rationale: The LLM tier is the one dependency with no abstraction; pin explicit versions (never -latest), monitor triage-suppression drift, and abstract behind a provider interface so a swap is config.

nodes.label: §12.9 Platform Substrate
nodes.rationale: Falcon is a multi-tenant runtime ingesting private source code and long-lived OAuth tokens from many companies into a shared coordinator — a framing that drives four hard requirements the earlier passes did not state.

nodes.label: §12.10 Capacity Model
nodes.rationale: The true hard ceiling is the Anthropic API tokens-per-minute/concurrency limit, not the infrastructure; the §12.6 throttle is a capacity dependency, not merely cost control.

nodes.label: §6.3 Deployment Topology
nodes.rationale: Merge/triage/coordinator are co-located in one session worker pinned by consistent hash on session_id, because the ≤7s budget can't absorb inter-service hops on every utterance and failover needs a single ownership boundary; synthesis runs off the hot path.

nodes.label: §15.1 Integration Reliability
nodes.rationale: Push-for-active (webhooks) + poll-for-historical resolves the F2.1 30-day-window vs same-day-freshness inconsistency; a silent sync failure is a correctness failure, not just availability.

nodes.label: Postgres RLS Tenant Isolation
nodes.rationale: Scoping in app code means one omitted predicate (including in a pgvector ANN query) leaks one company's code to another; RLS keyed on per-request tenant context makes isolation survive an application bug. App filtering is defense-in-depth, never the floor.

nodes.label: Dedicated Secrets Manager
nodes.rationale: Concentrated OAuth tokens across the whole customer base are a higher-value target than transcripts; kept out of the app DB under envelope encryption with per-tenant keys, rotation, and least-scope grants.

nodes.label: STT Circuit-broken Dependency
nodes.rationale: Every spoken word transits Deepgram in real time, so its failure is total input loss, not graceful degradation; circuit breaker fails over to AssemblyAI, and total loss buffers locally + marks an explicit gap.

nodes.label: Session-end Idempotent Finalization
nodes.rationale: The Redis→Postgres handoff of the Decision Record is a dual-write; an idempotent retryable BullMQ job reads the event log as source of truth and doesn't clear Redis until the Postgres commit confirms, so a partial failure never loses the meeting.

nodes.label: R12 Addressee Resolution Ambiguous
nodes.rationale: The R12 philosophy: surface a visible, degraded-but-honest state rather than a confident wrong one — wake every plausible candidate rather than guess.

nodes.label: R15 Private-artifact Leak on Shared Card
R22 Silent Capability Drift on Model Swap
R27 Silent Wrong Output from Integration/STT Failure
AD-1 Clock Reconstruction vs Server-arrival Ordering
nodes.rationale: Server-arrival ordering may eliminate the asymmetric-bias problem (R5) entirely and delete a whole subsystem — likely less code, not more; Phase 3 spike decides before the merge layer is built.

nodes.label: AD-2 Orchestration Substrate (LangGraph vs Hand-rolled)
nodes.rationale: Given the orchestration state layer is already hand-rolled (Redis event-sourcing + fencing tokens), a framework may add more friction than value.

nodes.label: AD-8 Agent Retrieval on the Hot Path
Phase 0 Validation
nodes.rationale: No code; record 10 real meetings and hand-write the cards — under 50% 'would this have changed the meeting?' means the thesis is wrong and no engineering fixes it.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Context Layer
nodes.rationale: The moat and architecture-independent — build it first, with no audio.

nodes.label: Phase 4 Mediation
nodes.rationale: The actual product; also where the injection suite, blame-neutral red-team, and A/B verdict-vs-both-sides are release gates.

nodes.label: Phase 5 Enterprise / Zoom
nodes.rationale: RTMS returns as the no-install enterprise escape hatch — an upgrade, not a foundation — only after Phase 4 proves the thesis.
